title: The bridged cross-polytope framework: unit-spring elastic constants in every dimension and an exact motion from the CaB6 boron net to face-centred cubic packing
description: Version 3, superseding v2 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23340326) and v1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23322080). For the periodic framework of regular cross-polytopes joined by bars (the same infinite framework, at a different bar length, as Borcea and Streinu 2021, Section 7; our counts are per cell of 2Z^n), we prove that with unit springs C44 = 0 (every stiffness component involving a cube-axis shear strain vanishes), C11/C12 = (n-1)^2 and the Poisson ratio for uniaxial stress along a cube axis is 1/(n^2-n-1), for every dimension n >= 3; the zero-mode and self-stress counts are lemmas following from existing periodic-rigidity machinery. In three dimensions we give an exact continuous motion, rational in one parameter over Q(sqrt2), that keeps every bar length, holds the octahedra in fixed orientation while the lattice deforms, raises the packing density strictly from 0.2233 to pi/sqrt18 and ends at face-centred cubic packing, with non-overlap proven. Secondary results: a radius-ratio identity and the exact CaB6-type packing maximum. Version 3 proves the point-group step of Theorem 2(e) that v2 asserted, marks the statements that rest on numerical checks or unreplayed search logs, and corrects the scope of the numerical rigidity check, the Borcea-Streinu comparison, several smaller statements, the repository address and the credits; no result changed. Corrections to the earlier versions: on some machines make verify in the v1.0.0 archive stops at verify-rigidity (n = 7, c = 0.3000) because of the default numpy.linalg.pinv cutoff; the exact formulas are unaffected and PR #8 fixed the numerical projection before v2.0.0. The v2.0.0 description's 'every shear modulus vanishes' should read C44 = 0, with the Poisson ratio for uniaxial stress along a cube axis. The archive contains the preprint (papers/incentre-lattice-v3.pdf; the v2 and v1 PDFs are kept unchanged), the interactive site, replayable verifiers and certificates.
